notes:
## New features & enhancements

- **Starting with Windows is now a switch in Settings.** **Settings → Service → Start when you sign in** shows whether the radio opens at sign-in, and changes it. It reads the machine rather than remembering an answer, so it cannot drift out of step with what is actually there.
- **That switch means one registry key — the first this app has ever written.** Every release until now promised there were none. Both readmes now say what this one is: `HKCU\Software\Classes\desksideradio`.
- It is a file association, not a start-up entry, and **nothing runs because it is there**. Uninstalling removes it.
- A page opened from a disk cannot put a shortcut in the Startup folder — no browser allows it, and none should. So the switch asks Windows to, through a handler that takes two fixed words and ignores everything else.
- What starts the radio at sign-in is still one shortcut in the Startup folder, which you can see and delete yourself.
- The first time you use the switch your browser asks permission, and names **Windows Based Script Host** rather than the radio. Tick **Always allow** *before* pressing Open, and it will not ask again.
- **The start-up script asks instead of assuming.** `Win - Start With Windows.cmd` is now **`Win - Start with Windows (On-Off).cmd`**. Run it and it says whether it is on and which folder that entry opens, then offers **R** to remove it or **P** to repoint it.
- That matters more than it sounds. An entry made from a copy unzipped somewhere temporary goes on opening *that* copy, and once it has gone you meet *Your file couldn't be accessed* at sign-in. **P** repoints it.
- The **Start when you sign in** and **Updates** panes are much shorter, and the word *guide* in each links straight to the section of the User Reference Guide that covers it.
- The sign-in pane now appears on macOS and Linux too, naming the route for each, rather than being hidden there.
- Tooltips wait a little longer before appearing.

## Bug fixes

- Two panes in Settings did not line up: an empty status line still took a row of the grid.
- The guide gave the permission dialog's two steps in the order that does not work — pressing Open closes the dialog, so a tick made afterwards never lands.
- The start-up script waited for a keypress on its removal path even when nothing was there to press one.
